shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures closed higher in choppy trading on Thursday, as a small US crop and a large import tender announced by Saudi Arabia helped bolster prices, market analysts said.

children: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures closed higher in choppy trading on Thursday, as a small US crop and a large import tender announced by Saudi Arabia helped bolster prices, market analysts said.

Saudi Arabia on Thursday announced it is seeking to buy 535,000 metric tons of wheat for shipment in November and December. Traders saw a sign that the recent price fall was stirring fresh demand after Saudi Arabia canceled its previous wheat tender on September 7 because of high prices.
Earlier in the session, the most-active CBOT wheat contract on a continuous basis
touched $6.70-3/4 a bushel, the contract's lowest price since August 14.
CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) closed 7 cents higher at $6.82-3/4 per bushel.
K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) ended up 4-1/2 cents at $7.37-1/2 a bushel, and Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) settled up 3-1/2 cents at $6.96-3/4 a bushel.
